name: @argszero/dsh-electron-marker-strip
description: Stop the Electron desktop host's own runtime marker from reaching the programs it spawns. Discussion #9920 (and its earlier duplicate #9599): launching an Electron-based editor from dsh makes it start as a Node interpreter and fail with a 502, because the editor process inherits ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 from the host that spawned it. The correct fix is one line in the shared scrub rule — SENSITIVE_ENV_PATTERN (packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/index.ts:47, /KEY|PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN/i) should carry ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE the way the tree's own desktop scripts already do (apps/desktop/scripts/ uses /KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|^NODE_OPTIONS$|^ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE$/iu) — and that line lives in the harness, not in a plugin. What a plugin can do is take the name out of the process the scrub reads: scrubbedParentEnv() (:66) walks Object.entries(process.env) at spawn time (:68), so deleting the name on mount covers every child spawned afterwards, whatever component spawns it, without touching the spawn path; the value is put back on disposal. Nothing in the tree depends on the leak — every in-tree launcher that needs the marker writes it explicitly AFTER the scrub (desktop-host/src/cli.ts:21, desktop-host/src/index.ts:36, desktop/src/node-environment.ts:15, host/open-in-app/src/resolver.ts:584, experimental/speech-to-text-sensevoice/src/recognizer.ts:265), which is why removing it from the base breaks nothing. This is a mitigation for an already-shipped desktop host, not the fix. Zero runtime dependencies.
